answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake and earn access to valuable tasks only after completing work that peers can verify. Reputation accumulates on that identity, so splitting into many fresh accounts does not multiply trust; each must independently post stake and build a track record. The island of newcomers may still participate, but its horizon is limited until evidence accrues. This costs an attacker capital, time, and the opportunity to reuse one proven identity’s nectar across a swarm.
